newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil off on moderating temp forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil off on moderating temp forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil continued its slide Wednesday afternoon after cold weather expected in the U.S. Northeast was forecasted not to be as drastic as first thought, dealers said.

"It's a combination of profit-taking after a phenomenal move to the upside, and it looks like it's not going to be as cold as originally expected," said Warren Tashnek, president of Fimat USA Futures in Houston. At 1344 EST, January heating oil was 1.04 cents lower a gallon at 72.50 cents. Support for prompt heat was pegged at around 72.15 to 72.20 using 38 percent Fibonacci retracement from Monday's high of 75.70.
January heating oil had risen 9.3 cents a gallon to Monday's high from last Wednesday's low of 66.40.

January crude was off 39 cents a barrel at $25.32 after it failed to break key resistance of $26.10, crude's post-Gulf War high made October 22. Traders also noted some rolling of positions out of January into February ahead of the front month contract expiration on Thursday.

"Some of this is on expiration, but it failed at around $26.00, so some weak length decided to take profits," said a dealer. January gasoline was off 0.97 cent a gallon at 68.80 cents in sympathy with the rest of the oil complex.

Weather Services Corp said an artic air mass which has pushed temperatures down 20 degrees below normal in some parts of the Midwest will moderate in the Northeast where temperatures will be at most eight degrees below normal by Saturday. The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world.
The National Weather Service said in its six to 10 day forecast that temperatures would average about normal in most of the Northeast.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
